newsitem.title: USA: Marzook says he expects to go to Jordan soon.
newsitem.headline: Marzook says he expects to go to Jordan soon.

text.p: Palestinian political activist Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook said on Thursday he expected to be sent to Jordan following Israel's decision to drop its request for his extradition.

"My understanding is that everything is done," Marzook told Reuters in an interview in the New York prison where he has been held without charge or trial since July 1995. "I think they are going to do something before Monday."

Israel announced earlier on Thursday it was suspending its 18-month-old extradition request for Abu Marzook, political leader of the militant Palestinian group Hamas, for reasons "relating to security and the prevention of terrorism."
Asked whether he believed he would be freed from U.S. jail and be sent to Jordan before a scheduled court hearing on Monday, Abu Marzook told Reuters: "Yes, this is my expectation."

Israel alleged that the Palestinian was responsible, as the head of Hamas' political wing, for attacks that killed scores of Israelis, but did not contend that he personally committed any acts of violence. Abu Marzook has denied involvement in any violence.
